tech.name: Gemini Decisions API (model gemini-decision-1)
tech.released: 2026-11-11, through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio; Google Cloud support coming soon
tech.status: available to developers; no-cost tier for prototyping
tech.one_line: Scores fixed options (yes/no, multiple choice 2-255, ordered rubric) instead of writing text: one input (text, images, audio, video, PDFs, up to 256K tokens) with up to 1,000 questions in one request, each answer with a confidence from 0 to 1; shared input billed once per request.

predecessor.name: Asking a chat model to write out each answer, one question per prompt, and parsing the words, with no number for how sure it was (the scene and the counted example are the episode's own)

claims.text: Gemini Decisions API, gemini-decision-1, launched Nov 11, 2026 via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio
One input across text, images, audio, video and PDFs (up to 256K tokens) with up to 1,000 independent questions
Scores candidate options instead of generating answer text, returning probabilities and confidence scores; $0.10 per 1M input tokens, zero output tokens billed
Yes/no, multiple choice and rubric questions mixed in one request
Every answer includes a confidence score from 0 to 1 so code can route ambiguous cases to a fallback or human reviewer
Multiple choice: 2 to 255 choices; rubric: ordered, starting at 0
Example shared input: a scanned PDF claim with damage photos
Shared input billed once per request no matter how many questions; each question adds its own instruction and criteria tokens
Nearly 5x cheaper across the shared benchmark suite than Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite with the Interactions API
Lowest calibration error on Google's benchmark suite
Gemini Notebook: up to 40% lower latency for everyday queries
Up to 1,000 questions in a single request (press confirmation)
A confidence score alone does not establish that an assessment is trustworthy (analyst)
Counted example (ours): 1 insurance claim, 20 questions; before 20 prompts sending the claim 20 times, now 1 call
